verses.text: Then Joshua called the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh,
and said to them, “You have kept all that Moses the servant of Yahweh commanded you, and have listened to my voice in all that I commanded you.
You have not left your brothers these many days to this day, but have performed the duty of the commandment of Yahweh your God.

Now Yahweh your God has given rest to your brothers, as he spoke to them. Therefore now return and go to your tents, to the land of your possession, which Moses the servant of Yahweh gave you beyond the Jordan.

Only take diligent heed to do the commandment and the law which Moses the servant of Yahweh commanded you, to love Yahweh your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to hold fast to him, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul.”
So Joshua blessed them, and sent them away; and they went to their tents.

Now to the one half-tribe of Manasseh Moses had given inheritance in Bashan; but to the other half gave Joshua among their brothers beyond the Jordan westward. Moreover when Joshua sent them away to their tents, he blessed them,

and spoke to them, saying, “Return with much wealth to your tents, with very much livestock, with silver, with gold, with brass, with iron, and with very much clothing. Divide the plunder of your enemies with your brothers.”

The children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh returned, and departed from the children of Israel out of Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilead, to the land of their possession, which they owned, according to the commandment of Yahweh by Moses.

When they came to the region about the Jordan, that is in the land of Canaan, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh built there an altar by the Jordan, a great altar to look at.

The children of Israel heard this, “Behold, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar in the border of the land of Canaan, in the region around the Jordan, on the side that belongs to the children of Israel.”
When the children of Israel heard of it, the whole congregation of the children of Israel gathered themselves together at Shiloh, to go up against them to war.
The children of Israel sent to the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, into the land of Gilead, Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest.
With him were ten princes, one prince of a fathers’ house for each of the tribes of Israel; and they were each head of their fathers’ houses among the thousands of Israel.
They came to the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, to the land of Gilead, and they spoke with them, saying,

“Thus says the whole congregation of Yahweh, ‘What trespass is this that you have committed against the God of Israel, to turn away today from following Yahweh, in that you have built yourselves an altar, to rebel today against Yahweh?
Is the iniquity of Peor too little for us, from which we have not cleansed ourselves to this day, although there came a plague on the congregation of Yahweh,
that you must turn away today from following Yahweh? It will be, since you rebel today against Yahweh, that tomorrow he will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.

However, if the land of your possession is unclean, then pass over to the land of the possession of Yahweh, in which Yahweh’s tabernacle dwells, and take possession among us; but don’t rebel against Yahweh, nor rebel against us, in building an altar other than Yahweh our God’s altar.
Didn’t Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the devoted thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel? That man didn’t perish alone in his iniquity.’”
Then the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered, and spoke to the heads of the thousands of Israel,
“The Mighty One, God, Yahweh, the Mighty One, God, Yahweh, he knows; and Israel shall know: if it was in rebellion, or if in trespass against Yahweh (don’t save us today),
that we have built us an altar to turn away from following Yahweh; or if to offer burnt offering or meal offering, or if to offer sacrifices of peace offerings, let Yahweh himself require it.
“If we have not out of concern done this, and for a reason, saying, ‘In time to come your children might speak to our children, saying, “What have you to do with Yahweh, the God of Israel?

For Yahweh has made the Jordan a border between us and you, you children of Reuben and children of Gad. You have no portion in Yahweh.”’ So your children might make our children cease from fearing Yahweh.
“Therefore we said, ‘Let’s now prepare to build ourselves an altar, not for burnt offering, nor for sacrifice;

but it will be a witness between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we may perform the service of Yahweh before him with our burnt offerings, with our sacrifices, and with our peace offerings;’ that your children may not tell our children in time to come, ‘You have no portion in Yahweh.’

“Therefore we said, ‘It shall be, when they tell us or our generations this in time to come, that we shall say, “Behold the pattern of Yahweh’s altar, which our fathers made, not for burnt offering, nor for sacrifice; but it is a witness between us and you.”’

“Far be it from us that we should rebel against Yahweh, and turn away today from following Yahweh, to build an altar for burnt offering, for meal offering, or for sacrifice, besides Yahweh our God’s altar that is before his tabernacle!”

When Phinehas the priest, and the princes of the congregation, even the heads of the thousands of Israel that were with him, heard the words that the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the children of Manasseh spoke, it pleased them well.

Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest said to the children of Reuben, to the children of Gad, and to the children of Manasseh, “Today we know that Yahweh is among us, because you have not committed this trespass against Yahweh. Now you have delivered the children of Israel out of Yahweh’s hand.”

Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, and the princes, returned from the children of Reuben, and from the children of Gad, out of the land of Gilead, to the land of Canaan, to the children of Israel, and brought them word again.

The thing pleased the children of Israel; and the children of Israel blessed God, and spoke no more of going up against them to war, to destroy the land in which the children of Reuben and the children of Gad lived.
The children of Reuben and the children of Gad named the altar “A Witness Between Us that Yahweh is God.”

footnotes.content: Joshua calls the three eastern tribes by name—Reubenites, Gadites, half-tribe of Manasseh. A leader's first act of farewell is to honor those who've served. These men fought alongside their brothers for years. Joshua sees them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He praises them: You have kept what Moses commanded, and you listened to my voice. That's the mark of a faithful servant—obedience to God's law and respect for His appointed leaders. It's the deepest tribute a commander can give.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You have not left your brothers. What a word. They could have gone home when their land was given. Instead they stayed through the long campaign, bearing witness that loyalty costs something and faithfulness shows up in the hard part.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now go rest. The Lord has given rest to your brothers. After years of war, to hear the word rest from your commander's mouth—that's a gift wrapped in favor. He sends them not just with permission but with blessing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yet as he blesses them to go, Joshua charges them: Love the Lord your God, walk in all His ways, keep His commandments, hold fast to Him, serve with all your heart and soul. This is the whole of the law—love so deep it shapes everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He blessed them and sent them away. That blessing—not just words but the weight of a leader's heart—goes with them on the long road home. A goodbye wrapped in favor is never quite goodbye.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Manasseh was split: Moses gave half of them Bashan on the east; Joshua gave the other half land with their brothers on the west. Even in the inheritances, God keeps His promises through different seasons and different hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Go home with much wealth—livestock, silver, gold, iron, clothing. Divide the plunder with your brothers. There's something tender in Joshua's mind here: he wants them rich, but not separate. Generosity with brothers is part of keeping faith with God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The three tribes turn from Shiloh toward Gilead, toward home across the Jordan. They've been faithful in the center. Now faithfulness will mean staying true when they're far from the tabernacle and from the sight of the main congregation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When they reach the Jordan, they build a great altar to look at. They're not hiding it. But before explanation comes, a visible monument to the distant—especially one large enough to see from far away—will look like trouble to those who are afraid.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The western Israelites hear: They've built an altar. Fear jumps in where knowledge ends. Are they breaking away? The gap between information and understanding is where trouble always grows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The whole congregation gathers to go to war. They move to protect the unity of God's people and His worship. It's zeal without mercy yet—the kind of response that asks questions after swords are drawn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They send Phinehas the priest, son of Eleazar. Phinehas has a reputation for zeal for the Lord's holiness. That choice says: we take this seriously, and we trust him to understand the heart of worship and covenant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: With Phinehas come ten princes, one from each tribe. This delegation carries weight—it's a national inquiry. All of Israel is watching.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They come to the three tribes in Gilead and speak with them. First comes the encounter. There's still room for words before swords fall.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What is this trespass? Are you turning from the Lord by building an altar to rebel? The law is clear: one altar in the place of the tabernacle. Their accusation is direct because the rule was plain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Is the iniquity of Peor too small? The memory of that place—where Israel turned to false gods and plague came—still cuts. They speak from hard-won faithfulness, guarding what the Lord has done.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If you rebel today, tomorrow the Lord will be angry with all of Israel. They're not hungry for power—they're afraid because the covenant binds them all together. One broken promise brings judgment on all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Phinehas offers a door: if your land is unclean, come back to us where the tabernacle is. But don't rebel by building another altar. There's a way forward if they'll listen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Remember Achan? One man's hidden sin brought judgment on the whole camp. Community is bound; one broken covenant affects all. The Lord takes His covenant seriously, and so must Israel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The eastern tribes answer. They speak to the heads of Israel's thousands—solemn, measured, ready to be heard because their conscience is clear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Mighty One, God, Yahweh—He knows, and Israel shall know: if this was rebellion or trespass, don't save us today. They invoke His name as witness. If they're lying, let judgment fall on them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If we built this altar for burnt offerings or meal offerings or sacrifices, let the Lord require it. They're saying: we didn't do that. Our intent was different.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We feared that in time to come your children might say to our children: What do you have to do with the Lord, the God of Israel? Distance across a river can become spiritual distance in the minds of the young.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Jordan has made a border between you and us. You might think: They have no portion in the Lord. So our children might stop fearing Him. That fear keeps them thinking generations ahead.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Therefore we said: Let's build an altar—not for burnt offering, not for sacrifice. The distinction is everything: this altar is not for worship, only for witness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: It will be a witness between us that we may perform the service of the Lord. A stone altar as a sign that though the Jordan divides the land, one Lord binds them together. It says: We belong to the covenant too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When they tell us or our generations this, we'll say: Behold the pattern of the Lord's altar, not for worship but a witness between us. They're thinking of stories told around fires generations from now.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Far be it from us that we should rebel. We built this not to divide but to declare that distance cannot separate us from the Lord or from His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When Phinehas and the princes hear their words, it pleased them well. Truth brings relief. The accusers are won over because the explanation is honest and the heart is right.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Phinehas says: Today we know the Lord is among us, because you didn't commit this trespass. The test has revealed faithfulness. You've delivered Israel from the Lord's hand. A word that turns war into peace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Phinehas and the princes return from Gilead to Canaan and bring word to the congregation. Good news travels fast when people long to hear it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: It pleased the children of Israel; they blessed God and spoke no more of war. Readers today hear an echo: how many conflicts dissolve when we pause to ask instead of assume, to listen instead of accuse? How many wars never happen because someone spoke truth first?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They named the altar: A Witness Between Us that Yahweh is God. One Lord across a river, across distance, across generations. That witness points to the only thing that can truly unite a divided people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
